title: weekly-sync-serving-runtime-infra-console-agenda-prep-2026-05-18
content:
Weekly sync prep (serving-runtime / infra / console) — 2026-05-18
Owner: Ethan Chen (notes + follow-ups)
Attendees (expected): Maya, Liam, Zoe, Ravi, Samira, ops on-call (TBD)
Duration: 45m
Location: #eng-serving-runtime Slack huddle / Zoom (link in calendar)

Objective: quick status, unblock key infra deploy, decide rollout policy for v1.8 kernel changes, action-item triage. Keep it tight — 5m per major topic + quick follow-ups.

Agenda (rough)
1) Quick round (5m)
- 1-line updates from each subteam: runtime, infra, console.
- Call out any urgent customer-facing incidents.

2) Infra / capacity update (10m) — Liam
- Current cluster capacity: gpu-pool-x at 72% avg (spiky at 90% p95) — still seeing scheduling delays for large-batch jobs.
- Autoscaler tweak deployed last week (rollout v2) — need to confirm if threshold change was effective.
- Open questions: revert threshold? Increase reserved burst for dedicated customers?
- Action: Liam to share pool utilization dashboard screenshot and proposed threshold numbers by EOD 2026-05-18.

3) Serving runtime: v1.8 kernel rollout plan (10m) — Maya
- Summary: new attention kernel improves 1-token latency ~8% on A10016 but increased mem fragmentation in long-seq workloads.
- Canary results: three canary shards, 48 hours, two regressions in kv-cache eviction path for seq>8k.
- Decision point: hold, partial rollout with fallback toggle, or full rollback.
- Notes: need an operator-visible rollback path in console (one-click) + runbook update.
- Action: Maya to propose canary -> staged rollout steps and emergency rollback playbook by 2026-05-20.

4) Console / rollouts UX (8m) — Zoe
- Request: add “toggle fallback model” control for canaries; surface ongoing canary stats (p50,p95,p99 latency + error rate).
- Small UI mock in Figma linked in notes. Need API to pull canary metrics from telemetry service (Ravi)
- Action: Zoe + Ravi to sync on API contract and timeframe (eta 2026-05-25).

5) Customer escalations / CS handoff (5m) — Ravi
- Two customers reported timeouts during burst window; both on dedicated capacity. Root cause suspected scheduling + kv-cache regen.
- Immediate mitigation: bump reserved burst capacity for affected tenants for 24h.
- Action: Ravi to open JIRA (JIRA-987) with ticket owner and link to incident notes. Ops to apply temporary bump and report.

6) Action-item review & AOB (7m)
- Quick scan of open action list from last week (see below).
- Any blockers that require cross-team escalation?

Open action items (from previous meetings) — quick notes
- ACTION-1: Maya to debug kv-cache eviction regression (owner: Maya) — in progress. Notes: repro case exists, working on smaller test harness. Due 2026-05-21.
- ACTION-2: Liam to evaluate autoscaler thresholds and propose safe defaults (owner: Liam) — pending. Due 2026-05-18.
- ACTION-3: Zoe to mock console rollback UX and share figma (owner: Zoe) — done, link in linked_artifacts.
- ACTION-4: Ethan to update runbook with emergency rollback steps (owner: Ethan) — draft in this doc. Due 2026-05-18.

Runbook / emergency rollback (draft notes)
- If canary shows kv-cache regression > 1% error or p99 latency > 2x baseline for two consecutive 5-min windows:
  - Step 1: Flip canary toggle to disable v1.8 kernel for affected shard(s) via console (one-click if available) or run helm rollback (ops).
  - Step 2: Re-route new traffic to previous kernel variant; monitor telemetry for 15 minutes.
  - Step 3: Notify CS + affected customers; create incident postmortem stub.
  - Step 4: Assign engineering owner to triage memory fragmentation root cause.
- Missing: exact console endpoint + RBAC gate — Zoe to propose.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal)
- Consider temporary increase in small-batch priority to reduce scheduling delays for low-latency customers. Could be a higher-priority queue + lower weight for batch jobs.
- Need a postmortem template for canary regressions (prompted by last week's slow response). Simple checklist + timeline.
- Evaluate adding a lightweight KV-cache health endpoint for canary verification (fast smoke test).

Linked artifacts / references
- Canary metrics dashboard: CONFLUENCE-RT/serving-runtime-canary-dashboard
- PR for kernel changes: GH-PR-4821
- Incident ticket: JIRA-987
- Console mock (Figma): figma.com/file/serving-console-rollback-mock (posted in Slack)

Prep tasks before sync (Ethan)
- Grab cluster utilization screenshot (Liam) — attach to meeting thread.
- Post concise summary of canary regressions in Slack #eng-serving-runtime.
- Update runbook section in this doc with any final wording after meeting.

QuickTODO (action item summary to paste into meeting notes)
- [ ] Liam: share pool utilization screenshot + threshold proposal (due 2026-05-18)
- [ ] Maya: propose staged rollout + rollback playbook (due 2026-05-20)
- [ ] Zoe + Ravi: sync on metrics API contract (due 2026-05-25)
- [ ] Ravi: open JIRA-987, ops to apply temporary burst bump (ASAP)
- [ ] Ethan: update runbook and post meeting notes (due 2026-05-18)

Scratchpad / stray thoughts
- If we need fast mitigation for customers, might ship hotfix on older kernel that reduces mem fragmentation (low risk). Need cost/benefit analysis.
- Longer term: add automated canary guardrails — fail open vs fail closed choices per tenant.

End of prep doc. Keep this doc as the source of truth for action items this week.

(Informal notes style intentionally — will clean up for runbook/pmo postmortem if needed.)
